column1: # Second-reader legacy registry -- a ratchet, never an escape hatch.
# Format: <card id> TAB <TDD layer> TAB <reason>.
# The line below is the ONLY place this registry states its own size, and
# `.board/validate.sh` derives every number in it from the entries and the
# recorded logs before comparing. `.board/README.md` must carry the identical
# sentence. Three texts once stated three different sizes for this one list;
# that is the drift this gate exists to refuse, so no other line here or in the
# README may count anything.
# count: 14 entry(ies) across 6 card(s), 6 distinct captured program(s)
# "Distinct captured program(s)" is smaller than "entry(ies)" on purpose and the
# gap is the honest measurement, not a rounding. `tests/acceptance/AUR-359.sh`
# and its three siblings dispatch four selector names onto ONE body, so the
# Contract/Integration/E2E records of those cards differ only in the selector
# they echo: a citation is not an execution, and this board counts executions.
# Closing the gap means giving each layer its own program, which is work on
# `tests/`, not on this registry.
# Cards that reached `done` before `.board/bin/second-reader` existed cite
# concrete Unit/Contract/Integration/E2E tests that no gate had ever executed.
# Every citation named below HAS now been executed:
# `.board/tests/second-reader-legacy/<card>.<layer>.raw.txt` holds the raw
# captured bytes, and `.board/validate.sh` recomputes the same facts from that
# log that it recomputes from a bundle-sealed observation -- the exact command,
# the exact selector, the locked image digest, the sha256 of the file that was
# read, the framed exit code, the match count, and the refusal of a selector
# that matched nothing.
# The single thing a legacy record cannot carry is the binding to the card's
# sealed CandidateIdentityV1: reopening a `done` evidence bundle is a
# coordinator act performed by three independent roles, and a builder that
# forged those digests would be manufacturing exactly the kind of self-declared
# evidence this board refuses. That missing binding is the reason each line
# below states, and it is printed on every validate.sh run as `board note:`.
# The registry only shrinks. `.board/validate.sh` refuses an entry for a card
# that is not in `done`, for a layer the card no longer cites, for a card/layer
# that already carries a sealed observation, and for any key outside the frozen
# cutover set compiled into `.board/validate.sh`. That last rule is what stops a
# card from joining this list in the same commit that moves it to `done`:
# growing the registry is a reviewed change to the validator, never a data edit.
AUR-020
column3: Bundle sealed before .board/bin/second-reader existed; the recorded run is green but is not bound to this card's sealed CandidateIdentityV1, which only a coordinator re-seal can restore.
